title: Add priority-aware kernel contention metrics and invocation SLA explainer
author: Maya Liu
description:
Context: production users have intermittent latency spikes during multi-tenant bursts that correlate with GPU kernel queueing and priority inversion at the runtime scheduler. Existing metrics showed aggregate kernel latency but not contention by invocation priority, making alerts noisy and root-cause analysis slow.

This change introduces a small, low-overhead telemetry path that surfaces kernel contention and queue depth broken down by invocation priority class and model shard. It also wires a new SLO explainer endpoint that maps per-route SLA violations to the dominant contention signal (kernel-queue, kv-cache-miss, batching-delay) to help on-call narrow down remediation steps faster.

What I changed: instrumented runtime scheduler to emit: priority.queue_depth, priority.kernel_hold_time_ms, kernel.preempt_count, and kernel-contention-ratio (0-1) with labels: tenant_id (hashed), model, priority_class (P0/P1/P2), shard_id. Added a lightweight aggregation rollup that computes 1m/5m/1h contention percentiles and a per-route derived metric route.sla_attribution that surfaces the top-1 contributing resource for a given SLA breach.

Why this is safe: metrics are opt-in via a feature flag (observability.priority_kernels) and sampling defaults to 1 in 50 invocations for priority=P2 to avoid high-cardinality explosion. Tenant identifiers are hashed and truncated to 8 chars for privacy. No user payload is collected.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag for two weeks on canaries, 24h perf/telemetry spike window, then gradual ramp to 30% of edge traffic, then to all. Dashboards and alert rules are included in this PR and will be staged in the observability namespace; they are muted until the flag is enabled.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler instrumentation + protobuf change (backwards compatible)
- [x] Metrics exporter + aggregation rollup
- [x] Route-level SLA explainer service and README
- [x] Dashboards (contour and heatmap panels) and alert playbook
- [x] Unit + integration tests for exporter and attribution logic
- [x] Security review and PII audit

Testing and validation: unit tests and local integration run in CI; we exercised the feature on the perf-canary cluster with synthetic load that reproduces priority inversion and observed the contention ratio spike align with increased per-invocation kernel_hold_time_ms. The SLA explainer returned correct top contributors for 92% of synthetic failures in our end-to-end replay.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids adding high-cardinality route tags to the base metrics. If customers opt into per-route attribution we emit a derived aggregated metric (route.sla_attribution) that is pre-aggregated server-side to reduce cardinality. Full docs for the feature flag lives in docs/observability/priority-kernels.md.

review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Can we avoid emitting tenant_id for P0 to prevent accidental cardinality spikes? — Responded: Maya Liu: yes — we only emit hashed tenant_id for P0 as well, but we bucket high-cardinality tenants into 'top' and 'others' server-side.

Sophie Patel: The aggregation window of 1m/5m/1h is good, but we should expose a 10s fast-path for alerting on extreme contention. — Responded: Maya Liu: added a 10s emergency gauge with sampling limited to priority=P0, P1 and can be toggled via flag.
Ravi Kapoor: Confirmed PII audit and KMS usage for stored rollups. Approving after security note added. — Responded: Maya Liu: security note added and audit doc linked.
release_notes: Add opt-in priority-aware kernel contention metrics and a route SLA explainer service. New dashboards and alerts provide per-priority visibility and reduce noisy SLA alerts by attributing breaches to kernel contention, KV-cache misses, or batching delays. Feature is behind feature flag and off by default.
